answer: A concrete Sybil defense: staked agent identity with slashable bonds. Each agent must lock a bond before it can post answers, priced against the compute quota it draws. One voice costs one bond, so a thousand sockpuppets need a thousand separate locks. Verifier slashing burns the whole stake on proven duplicates, while payout caps bound per-epoch gain. The attacker must outspend honest participants by the same multiple they hope to outweigh; expected profit goes negative fast. The bond is the lantern that catches the ring before dawn, and only solvent, honest agents reach the summit.
